newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cambior sees no Metates gold mine start-up yet.
newsitem.headline: Cambior sees no Metates gold mine start-up yet.

text.p: The massive Mexican Metates gold mine will probably not start producing inside the next three to four years, a Cambior Inc. project manager involved in the property said on Tuesday.
"I do not think we have any hopes it (production) is going to happen in the next three to four years at the earliest," Gary Parkison told the Mexico Mining 1997 conference in Puerto Vallarta.
Metates is one of the largest gold resources discovered in Mexico and is still under study.

Cambior is in a 50-50 joint venture in the project with Mexican miners Luismin SA, the mining unit of Corporacion Industrial Sanluis. One study has estimated proven and probable reserves at 10.5 million ounces of gold.

Parkison said drilling has found gold levels of between 1.40 and 1.90 grammes/tonne in the main zone and 1.0 to 2.1 grammes/ tonne in the northern zone. He said Cambior had spent $12.5 million on the project to date since their joint venture with Luismin in 1993.

Parkison said the mine, in one of the more inaccessible parts of the Sierra Madre Occidental mountains in northwest Durango state, would most probably have to have link roads built to make it operable.
Cambior and Luismin, he said, continued to classify Metates as "a world-class gold mine."
